name: codeg_help
description: Discover Codeg Host Control capabilities only when the user's request needs them. This is the small, read-only gateway for persistent Session lifecycle actions. Call it before codeg_use when you need an action's exact input contract. The returned catalog is filtered by the current Session's live feature and host policy. Caller identity is derived by Codeg; never try to provide your own Session id or a from/source field.

query.description: Optional words to filter action names and descriptions. Omit to list every currently available action.

action.description: Optional exact action id such as session.rename.

name: codeg_use
description: Execute one action discovered through codeg_help. Pass the exact action id and an input object matching its catalog schema. Codeg strictly validates the action-specific input again in the Host Core. Do not add from, source_session_id, current_session_id, or a request id: Codeg derives caller identity from the per-launch companion token and mints an idempotency key from this MCP call.

input.description: Action-specific arguments from codeg_help. Unknown fields are rejected by the Host Core.

name: check_user_feedback
description:
IMPORTANT: This tool gives you the ability to receive the user's real-time guidance while you work, preventing you from going down the wrong path and wasting effort. The user can type corrections, new requirements, or hints at any time during your turn — but you will NEVER see them unless you call this tool. Without it, you could spend minutes on work the user has already tried to redirect.

When to call:
- After thinking through your approach but BEFORE starting implementation — the user may have clarified requirements.
- Before making a significant decision (choosing an architecture, picking which files to modify, deciding on an approach) — the user may prefer a different direction.
- After completing a sub-task and before moving to the next step — the user may want to adjust priorities.
- When you pause to plan or organize your next steps — a natural checkpoint to read any pending guidance.

This is a quick, non-blocking snapshot that returns instantly. It either returns the user's messages (treat as HIGH-PRIORITY steering and adjust immediately) or an empty result (continue your current plan). Call it proactively — do not wait to be asked.

name: ask_user_question
description: Ask the user one or more multiple-choice questions and BLOCK until they answer. The questions render as interactive cards above the user's input box; this call returns only once the user submits their choices (or dismisses the card). Use ONLY when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make — one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults (e.g. which approach, which format, which library, which of several files). Do NOT use it to ask 'should I proceed?' or to confirm an obvious default, and do NOT use it for open-ended questions that aren't a small set of discrete choices. The user can always pick 'Other' and type a custom answer, so don't add your own 'Other' option. If you want to recommend a choice, put it first and append ' (Recommended)' to its label. Prefer ONE call with a few related questions over many sequential calls.

questions.description: 1-4 questions to ask in this single call.

question.description: The full question shown to the user.

header.description: Short category label (≤ 12 chars) shown as a chip, e.g. 'Approach', 'Format'.

multiSelect.description: If true, the user may select multiple options; otherwise it's a single choice.

label.description: Concise choice text. Append ' (Recommended)' to the first option to recommend it.

description.description: What this choice means or its trade-off.

name: get_session_info
description: Look up a session/conversation the user referenced in their message and return what it is: its title, which agent ran it, its status, workspace folder, git branch, model, message count, and token-usage stats — and, on request, a compact view of its most recent messages. RECOGNIZING A MENTIONED SESSION: the user can @-mention a past session directly in their message — it appears as a Markdown link `[Session title](codeg://session/<number>)`, whose text is that session's title and whose `<number>` is codeg's internal conversation id (e.g. `[Fix auth](codeg://session/214)` is the session titled 'Fix auth'). Such a mention IS the user pointing you at that session as context. This tool is read-only inspection: it does not send a mailbox letter and does not post to a Room. Use send_message for private mail and post_room to @mention in a Room. Call this whenever what that session is about or what happened in it matters to the request (e.g. to continue its work, build on its results, answer questions about it, or summarize it). If the message mentions several sessions, make one call per session. Pass the NUMBER from the reference as `session_id` (it is codeg's internal conversation id, NOT the agent's own session id). A session that no longer exists returns a `found: false` result you can act on — it is not an error.

session_id.description: The number in the mentioned session's `codeg://session/<number>` link (codeg's internal conversation id). For example, given the mention `[Fix auth](codeg://session/214)`, pass 214.

max_messages.description: How many of the session's most recent turns to include as compact text. Defaults to 20; pass 0 for metadata only (faster, no transcript read). Capped at 200.

name: list_sessions
description: Find other persistent Sessions managed by Codeg so you can address them by stable Session id. Use this when the user asks you to consult, notify, or collaborate with an existing Session but has not already supplied a codeg://session/<id> reference. Results exclude this calling Session and unsent drafts, and include the title, Harness, workspace, status, and last activity needed to disambiguate duplicate names. A title or role is only a human-facing selector. Pass the returned numeric session_id to send_message for private mail, or to post_room.mention_session_ids to tap that Session in a Room. Do not treat a codeg://session/<id> badge in the current user turn as an automatic letter — that badge is context for get_session_info unless the user asked you to write mail or post in a Room.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive filter over title, Session id, Harness, workspace name, and workspace path. Omit for the most recently active Sessions.

limit.description: Maximum results. Defaults to 50; narrow query instead of requesting a huge address book.

name: send_message
description: Send a durable private mailbox letter. Letters have a short title and a body. The first delivery copies title plus body into the target's prompt (truncated if long). Call read_message(event_id) to mark the letter read and to fetch any truncated remainder. Time-out reminders are title-only and do not repeat the body. This is not a Room post — use post_room for shared Rooms. priority=high (default) tells the target now: steer into the running turn when that channel exists, otherwise stop the turn and deliver; a closed Session is started. priority=normal waits for the target's next ordinary turn — the letter is still for the Agent. For a private reply or a follow-up supplement on the same thread, target the same peer and set reply_to_event_id. Omitting reply_to_event_id starts a new thread.

target_session_ids.description: One or more Session ids to receive this private letter. Recipients cannot see each other.

title.description: Short letter title, like an email subject. Shown in list_inbox and system reminders. Do not put the full body here.

content.description: The letter body. Copied into the first delivery prompt (truncated if long). list_inbox stays titles only. read_message returns the full body and marks the letter read.

priority.description: How soon the target Agent should see this letter. high (default): notify now — steer into the running turn if supported, otherwise stop that turn and deliver; start/resume a closed Session. normal: keep it in the mailbox until the next ordinary turn; a closed Session is still started so that turn can happen. Both are Agent mail. delivery_mode=queue/deliver_only is a legacy alias for high/normal.

delivery_mode.description: Legacy alias. queue = priority high; deliver_only = priority normal. Prefer `priority`.

delivery_hint.description: Optional non-destructive hint for queue mode. steer_if_supported tries proven native steering only while the target is busy; unsupported, stale, oversized, or idle cases remain in the durable queue. It never interrupts the target.

expects_reply.description: Whether the target should send a linked reply after finishing. Defaults to true; set false for FYI/notifications.

reply_to_event_id.description: Event id of the letter this continues. Required for the first reply and for later supplements on the same thread (point at the inbound event_id, or at your last send in that thread). Omitting it creates a new root with no parent. Private follow-ups must target the same peer as that letter. The first linked reply clears expects_reply debt; later supplements stay on the thread and do not reopen it unless expects_reply is true again.

name: list_inbox
description: List this Session's Agent mailbox. box=inbox (default) lists received letters; box=sent lists letters this Session sent, with the same filter words applied to the recipient (unread: they have not received it; awaiting_reply: they still owe the reply). Use peer_session_id to see only the exchange with one Session. Results are newest first and include the letter title only — call read_message with event_id to mark a received letter read and to open the full body. Listing does not mark mail as read. A human opening the Session never consumes this mailbox.

box.description: inbox (default): letters this Session received. sent: letters this Session sent — use with filter=awaiting_reply to see who still owes you a reply.

filter.description: open (default): unread or still expecting a reply. unread: not yet received (by this Agent for inbox, by the recipient for sent). awaiting_reply: reply obligation is still open. all: every non-dismissed letter in the box.

peer_session_id.description: Only letters exchanged with this Session id: the sender for inbox, the recipient for sent.

limit.description: Maximum letters to return. Defaults to 20; raise only if you must page.

name: read_message
description: Open one inbound Agent mailbox letter by event_id and return its title and full body. Opening marks the letter read for this Agent so unread reminders stop, including when the first delivery already showed the body. It does not send a reply and does not clear a reply obligation. If expects_reply is true, answer with send_message targeting from_session_id and setting reply_to_event_id. Further supplements to the same letter must also set reply_to_event_id; omitting it starts a new thread. Do not invent event ids. Do not use this for Room posts — call read_room instead.

event_id.description: The event_id from list_inbox or from a collaboration reminder/envelope.

name: list_rooms
description: List shared Rooms this Session already belongs to. Use this to find a room_id before read_room or post_room. Results include title and member count. Creating a Room or adding members is Host Control (room.create / room.add_member), not this tool.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive filter over Room title and room_id. Omit for recently active Rooms.

name: read_room
description: Read a shared Room timeline this Session belongs to. Returns members and recent posts with full bodies. Room posts never appear in list_inbox. A Room mention envelope already includes that post's body; call this with the given room_id for surrounding posts. Reply with post_room using the same room_id and reply_to_event_id; do not send_message a private letter unless asked.

room_id.description: The Room id from list_rooms or a Room mention envelope.

limit.description: Maximum timeline events, oldest first. Defaults to 50.

name: post_room
description: Post to a shared Room this Session already belongs to. Every member can read the body on the Room timeline. Omit mention_session_ids (and mention_all=false) for a record-only post that wakes nobody. Structured mentions create deliveries and may start a turn. Do not expect free-text @names in the body to wake anyone — use mention_session_ids, mention_all, or mention_human. File references in the body are context only. This is not private mail — do not use send_message. For a reply or supplement, set the same room_id and reply_to_event_id.

room_id.description: The Room to post in. The caller must already be a member.

content.description: The post body. Visible to every Room member on the timeline.

title.description: Optional short title. Unlike mailbox letters, Room posts may omit this.

mention_session_ids.description: Sessions to @mention. Empty or omitted = record-only. Mentions must already be members. An archived member is still named on the public post but is not woken.

mention_all.description: Mention every other Session member. Does not mention the human operator. Archived members are named on the post, not woken. Prefer explicit mention_session_ids unless @all is intended.

mention_human.description: Tap the human operator's shoulder (@human / @user). Records mention_human on the public Room post. Does not wake a Session. Not a file reference.

priority.description: How soon mentioned Sessions should see this. high (default when anyone is mentioned): notify now. normal: wait for the next ordinary turn. Record-only posts ignore this because nobody is delivered.

expects_reply.description: Whether mentioned Sessions should answer in the same Room. Defaults to false.

reply_to_event_id.description: Event id this post continues. Required for replies and later supplements on the same Room thread. Omitting it starts a new root.

name: create_automation
description: Save a codeg Automation: a reusable job — a prompt plus a target project — that codeg runs on a cron schedule (or on demand) without anyone present. Use it when the user asks for work that should REPEAT or happen at a TIME rather than right now: 'every morning', 'each Monday', 'nightly', 'every 30 minutes', 'before standup', 'set up a recurring …'. Do NOT use it for work the user wants done in this conversation — just do that work. Each run starts a fresh headless session in its own worktree with no memory of this chat, so `prompt` must be completely self-contained: state the goal, the relevant paths, and what a finished run looks like. Creating an automation does not run it now; the tool returns the id and the next fire time so you can tell the user when it will first go off. The user can edit, disable, run, or delete it on the Automations page.

name.description: Short label shown in the automations list, e.g. 'Nightly dependency audit'.

prompt.description: The self-contained instruction each run executes. The run cannot see this conversation, so spell out the goal, the paths, and the definition of done.

cron.description: 5-field cron, and only 5 fields: `min hour day-of-month month day-of-week`, e.g. `0 9 * * 1-5` for weekdays at 09:00. Day-of-week is POSIX (0 and 7 are both Sunday). A seconds field is NOT supported and is rejected. Interpreted in `timezone`. OMIT this to create a manual automation the user runs on demand from the Automations page.

timezone.description: IANA zone the cron is read in, e.g. 'Asia/Shanghai'. Defaults to the machine's own zone — omit it unless the user names a different one.

action.description: What a fire does. 'launch_session' (default) runs the prompt immediately in a headless agent session. 'enqueue_task' instead drops a card on the user's to-dos for the board's queue to pick up — use it when the user wants scheduled work to land somewhere they review rather than run unattended.

agent_type.description: Which local agent runs it (e.g. 'claude_code', 'codex'). Defaults to the target project's configured agent — omit unless the user asks for a specific one.

folder_path.description: Absolute path of the target project. Defaults to the project this conversation is in; pass it only to target a different project already open in codeg.

enabled.description: Whether the schedule is live right away. Defaults to true; pass false to save it switched off.

name: create_work_task
description: Queue a card on codeg's to-dos. A task is a unit of work an agent later executes on its own branch/worktree, then hands back for the user to review and merge. Use it when the user wants work PARKED rather than done now — 'add a task to…', 'put this on the board', 'we should also fix X later' — or when you are splitting a large request into reviewable pieces and the user asked for that. Do NOT use it to do the thing the user just asked you to do in this conversation, and do NOT queue a task per trivial step. The executing agent starts cold with no view of this chat, so `prompt` must carry the full briefing. The tool returns the task id; the user tracks it in their to-dos.

title.description: Short card title, e.g. 'Migrate auth middleware to the new session API'.

prompt.description: The self-contained instruction the executing agent receives: the goal, the relevant files/paths, constraints, and what done looks like.

agent_type.description: Which local agent should run this task (e.g. 'claude_code', 'codex'). Omit to inherit the board's configured default.

folder_path.description: Absolute path of the target project. Defaults to the project this conversation is in; pass it only to target a different project already open in codeg.

name: task_progress
description: Report a short progress milestone for the work task you are executing. It shows up on the task's board card and timeline in real time, so the user can follow along without opening the session. Call it at meaningful checkpoints — finished exploring, tests passing, starting the refactor — not for every small step. Fire-and-forget: it never blocks your work and returns immediately.

message.description: One-line progress note, e.g. 'tests passing, starting cleanup'.

name: task_complete
description: Report the final outcome of the work task you are executing. Call it once, just before you end your reply. Pass verdict 'success' when the change is done and ready to review, 'needs_review' when it works but a human should double-check something specific (say what in the summary), or 'blocked' when you could not complete the task (the summary must say why). The task settles when your turn ends: success and needs_review send it to review, blocked marks it failed. If you never call this tool the task still settles normally from your turn's end.

verdict.description: How the task ended from your point of view.

summary.description: Short result summary shown on the task card: what changed, and anything the reviewer should look at.
